title: Mirror Trading International: 29,421 BTC 'forex bot' Ponzi — the largest Bitcoin fraud charged by the CFTC
summary: South Africa's Mirror Trading International took at least 29,421 BTC from investors (May 2018–March 2021) for a forex 'trading bot' the FSCA found never traded as sold. A 2023 US default judgment ordered $1.73B restitution plus a record $1.73B penalty; a South African court declared MTI an unlawful Ponzi scheme. The only official claims channel is the liquidators' portal mticlaims.co.za.

entities.vendor: Mirror Trading International Proprietary Limited (in liquidation), Stellenbosch, South Africa

impact.lossNative: At least 29,421 BTC accepted from participants (CFTC, valued at over $1,733,838,372 as of March 2021); FSCA investigation reported ~23,000 BTC unaccounted for
impact.victims: At least 23,000 US participants per the CFTC; ~300,000 members worldwide reported by Carte Blanche's investigation (via Moonstone) and Webber Wentzel; other coverage reports ~100,000

timeline.event: MTI begins soliciting bitcoin for a purported commodity pool, claiming a proprietary 'bot' trades leveraged forex, and recruits through websites, social media, and a multi-level referral program.

South Africa's FSCA publicly warns that MTI is not licensed to provide financial services, and says it cannot confirm that the more-than-R2.9-billion in client funds MTI claims to hold actually exists.
Amid mounting withdrawal problems, the FSCA reiterates that MTI is unlicensed and that it believes the operation is illegal.
MTI stops honoring withdrawals and collapses; the Western Cape High Court places it in provisional liquidation (exact order date widely reported as 29 December 2020 — see claims).

The FSCA finalizes its investigation, concluding — per its head of investigations — that 'MTI was a scam and that there is no evidence of trading by an AI bot as it was sold to investors,' and opens a criminal case with the Commercial Crime Unit.
The Western Cape High Court grants a final liquidation order winding up MTI, converting the provisional order of 29 December 2020; the joint liquidators proceed to trace and recover assets.
Founder and CEO Cornelius Johannes Steynberg, a fugitive from South African law enforcement, is detained in Brazil on an INTERPOL arrest warrant, where he remained as of the 2023 US judgment.

The CFTC files fraud and registration charges against Steynberg and MTI in the US District Court for the Western District of Texas — the largest fraudulent scheme involving bitcoin charged in any CFTC case.
Default judgment against Steynberg: $1,733,838,372 in restitution plus a $1,733,838,372 civil monetary penalty — the highest in CFTC history — with permanent trading and registration bans.

The Western Cape High Court (Bester NNO and Others v MTI, [2023] ZAWCHC 38) declares that MTI — in liquidation since mid-2021 — conducted an unlawful Ponzi-type and pyramid scheme, and that all agreements between MTI and its investors are void from the outset, exposing net winners to clawback.

Liquidators report 1,281 BTC recovered and unfrozen from MTI's broker FX Choice, with distributions expected to run for at least another 2–3 years and a court question pending on how claims are valued.

England and Wales formally recognizes the South African liquidation as a foreign main proceeding in December 2023; the US (Chapter 15), Australia, Belgium, and Canada have granted similar recognition (the source gives no dates for these), letting liquidators pursue assets and net winners abroad.

Brazilian media report that Steynberg, under house arrest in Brazil's Goiás state, died on 22 April 2024, with a death certificate reportedly citing a massive bilateral pulmonary thromboembolism; South Africa's Hawks say they are verifying the reports, and faked-death suspicions circulate — see claims.

Moneyweb reports the estate is shrinking: of the ~R1.1 billion realised from the bitcoin recovered via FX Choice, only about R550 million remained by December 2024, with no dividends yet paid to creditors; R120.4 million had gone to liquidators' fees and R283 million to SARS — see claims.

affected: Anyone who deposited bitcoin with MTI between May 2018 and March 2021 — net losers claim through the South African liquidation
Net winners — members who withdrew more than they deposited; the void-from-the-outset ruling exposes them to clawback by liquidators in multiple countries
US participants — covered by the CFTC restitution order, but the CFTC cautions that orders requiring payment 'may not result in the recovery of any money lost'
All former MTI members — prime targets for follow-on 'recovery' scams referencing their MTI balances
notAffected: Anyone who never sent bitcoin to MTI — watching promos, joining Telegram groups, or holding an unfunded account put nothing at risk
Users of legitimate 'copy trading' or 'mirror trading' features at licensed brokers — the name overlaps, the company does not
Members who already filed with the liquidators owe nothing further to anyone to keep a claim alive — no fee 'activates' or 'releases' a claim
actions: If you deposited bitcoin with MTI, the only official claims channel is the joint liquidators' portal at mticlaims.co.za (administered with Investrust; the liquidators' back-office reference copy is at live.mticlaims.co.za). File there — the portal calculates claims from deposits minus withdrawals in MTI's records.

Gather your evidence now: MTI back-office screenshots, bitcoin transaction IDs, deposit addresses, and withdrawal records. Claims are verified against MTI's account data, and your own records fill the gaps.

Treat every unsolicited 'MTI recovery' offer as a scam. The liquidators do not cold-call, do not work through WhatsApp or Telegram, and do not charge upfront fees to 'release' bitcoin. Anyone promising your coins back for a fee is running the second half of the scam.

US participants: report your loss to the CFTC (https://www.cftc.gov/complaint) and the FBI's IC3 (https://www.ic3.gov). The $1.73B restitution order exists, but the CFTC itself cautions it may not result in recovery — never pay anyone claiming they can unlock it for you.

If you withdrew more than you put in, expect a clawback: the Western Cape High Court voided all MTI transactions from the outset and liquidators are pursuing net winners internationally. Get independent legal advice before responding to a demand.

Expect distributions to take years, not weeks. Reported recoveries so far (1,281 BTC from MTI's broker) are a fraction of the 29,421 BTC taken in — any message claiming your 'full balance is ready for release' is fraudulent.

claims.claim: The court found that the defendants, directly or indirectly, took for themselves every bitcoin participants entrusted to the pool; per the CFTC's default judgment, Steynberg is liable for fraud in retail forex transactions, fraud as an associated person of a commodity pool operator, and registration violations.
claims.attribution: CFTC press releases 8696-23 and 8549-22 (default judgment — Steynberg did not appear to contest the charges)

claims.claim: Steynberg has been detained in Brazil on an INTERPOL arrest warrant since December 2021 and is a fugitive from South African law enforcement; his current custody status and any criminal outcome after April 2023 are not covered by our fetched sources.

MTI attracted roughly 300,000 members across 200+ countries per Carte Blanche's investigation (as reported by Moonstone) and Webber Wentzel's insolvency analysis; other coverage reports ~100,000 members. Separately, the FSCA reported ~23,000 BTC unaccounted for and opened a criminal case with the Commercial Crime Unit.
claims.attribution: Member/country figures: Carte Blanche via Moonstone, and Webber Wentzel (the figure is contested and is not an FSCA finding); BTC-unaccounted and criminal-case facts: FSCA as reported by Moonstone

claims.claim: The provisional liquidation order was granted on 29 December 2020 in the Western Cape High Court.
claims.attribution: Widely reported in liquidation coverage; the fetched primary and law-firm sources confirm the provisional liquidation but not the exact order date

claims.claim: Liquidators recovered 1,281 BTC from MTI's broker FX Choice, expect distributions to continue for at least 2–3 more years, and had received claims from 7,903 of roughly 15,500 unique participants as of October 2023; a court question on claim valuation (deposit date vs closure date) was pending.
claims.attribution: Mariblock reporting on the liquidators' statements (published 4 October 2023)

claims.claim: Steynberg died on 22 April 2024 while under house arrest in Goiás state, Brazil, with a death certificate reportedly citing acute respiratory failure and a massive bilateral pulmonary thromboembolism; South Africa's Hawks said they were verifying the reports before the NPA would consider dropping charges, and faked-death suspicions persist in South African coverage.
claims.attribution: Brazilian press reports relayed by Moneyweb and Moonstone (April 2024); the Hawks confirmed only that they were validating the news

claims.claim: Of the ~R1.1 billion realised from the recovered MTI bitcoin, only about R550 million remained by December 2024, with no dividends yet paid to creditors; R120.4 million had been paid in liquidators' fees (per the June 2023 liquidation and distribution account) and R283 million to SARS.
